title: Transformations
examples: What is the difference between translating and reflecting a shape?
Can you show me how to rotate a shape around a point?
If I enlarge a shape by a negative scale factor, what happens?

explain.say: Today we will learn about geometric transformations. A transformation moves a shape to a new place. We will look at four main types of moves.
First, let us look at reflection. A reflection creates a mirror image of the original shape. The line of reflection acts like a mirror.
Next is translation. A translation slides the shape across the plane. It moves every point the same distance and in the same direction.
Rotation turns the shape around a fixed point. You must know the centre point and the angle of turn. Think of turning a clock hand.
Finally, we have enlargement. This changes the size of the shape. The scale factor tells us how much bigger or smaller it becomes. A negative scale factor flips it.

faq.q: What is the difference between reflection and translation?
faq.a: A reflection flips the shape across a line, like looking in a mirror. A translation simply slides the shape without flipping it.
asks: How is a reflection different from sliding?
Does a translation ever flip a shape?

faq.q: When do I need to use a rotation?
faq.a: You use rotation when you need to turn the shape around a specific point. You must know the centre point and the angle.
asks: What is the centre point for rotation?
Do I need an angle for turning?

faq.q: What does a scale factor of negative one mean?
faq.a: A negative scale factor means the shape is enlarged and then reflected through the origin. It flips it across both axes.
asks: What does a negative scale factor do?
Is it always a reflection when the factor is negative?

faq.a: No, only reflection, rotation, and translation are rigid. Enlargement changes the size, so it is not rigid.
asks: Which transformations keep the size the same?

faq.q: Do I need coordinates for every transformation?
faq.a: Yes, knowing the coordinates helps you find the exact new position. For example, you need a line or a centre point.
asks: Can I do this without coordinates?
What information is needed to start?

facts: Reflection creates a mirror image across a line.
Translation slides a shape without changing its orientation.
Rotation turns a shape around a fixed centre point.
Enlargement changes the size using a scale factor.
A scale factor of one means no change in size.

quiz.say: A shape moves from point A to point B by sliding it straight across the grid.
quiz.why: Sliding the shape in a straight line is the definition of a translation.

wrong.1: Reflection involves flipping the shape across a line, not just sliding it.
wrong.2: Rotation requires turning the shape around a specific point, not just moving it straight.
wrong.3: Enlargement changes the size, but this question only describes the movement.

quiz.say: A shape is turned 90 degrees anti-clockwise around the origin.
quiz.why: Turning a shape around a point by a specific angle is called a rotation.

wrong.0: Enlargement changes the size, but this question only describes the turning action.
wrong.2: Translation only involves sliding the shape, not turning it.
wrong.3: Reflection creates a mirror image, which is different from turning it.

quiz.say: A shape is made larger by a scale factor of two.
quiz.why: Changing the size of a shape using a scale factor is the process of enlargement.

wrong.0: Rotation turns the shape but does not change its size.
wrong.1: Translation only moves the shape without changing its size or shape.
wrong.3: Reflection keeps the size the same; it only flips the shape.
